#### What this PR does / why we need it:
Add Validation to versioned feature specs to ensure:
* deprecated feature always has a prior state
* versions strictly increase in `VersionedSpecs` list
* no regression in feature stability level

This is better than linter/unit test, because it is ensuring all features follow the same rules, not just limited to k/k.

issue_context.title: Ensure emulation-version works with feature gates that progress to false
comments:
IIRC we have seen feature gates go from off-by-default to on-by-default to _oops, we've done it again_ back to off-by-default and eventually end up stable (feature implicitly on). It's rare but we need to support this kind of transition.

/sig architecture
too

> go from off-by-default to on-by-default to oops, we've done it again back to off-by-default

in all the cases like that I know of, we realized in a later release a beta feature regressed something badly enough the safest fix was to demote back to disabled by default, and we backported the disablement to the previous release branch. In that case, the enablement state at HEAD of master should represent the enablement state at HEAD of the minor release branches, including any post 1.x.0 enablement changes.

Emulation version only has minor granularity and should represent our present-day understanding of the latest state of the feature gate in each previous minor.

> Emulation version only has minor granularity and should represent our present-day understanding of the latest state of the feature gate in each previous minor.

Yeah this case seems fine since the state at HEAD is the most accurate representation and changes would be backported. 

> I think emulation version assumes gate state in prior releases is false, and progresses to true in later releases.

This is definitely a problem. When the emulated version is set to prior to a feature's introduction, we assume the feature is in "[pre-alpha](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/component-base/featuregate/feature_gate.go#L607-L611)" state which has the feature set to off. Instead having to remember to set that deprecated features should be in a on state before the deprecation, I think it will be better to special case deprecated features that if the emulation version is prior to the introduction of the deprecation AND has no other transitions, the feature default state is on. 

Obviously we could still have some cases like 

```
{Version: version.MustParse("1.32"), Default: false, PreRelease: featuregate.Alpha},
{Version: version.MustParse("1.33"), Default: true, PreRelease: featuregate.Beta},
{Version: version.MustParse("1.34"), Default: false, PreRelease: featuregate.Deprecated}
```

that should still respect that pre 1.32 should default to false. 

I don't see explicitly that all [deprecation transitions](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/deprecation-policy/#deprecation) from true -> false, but it seems to be implicit from the documentation and I don't see any exceptions currently. (though haven't looked at historical cases)

- alpha -> deprecated: technically could just immediately remove feature but pre-alpha behavior should remain false
- beta -> deprecated: Betas are not guaranteed on by default so either true -> false or false -> false. pre-beta behavior should still be false
- n/a -> deprecated introduced: goes from true to false

> Instead having to remember to set that deprecated features should be in a on state before the deprecation, I think it will be better to special case deprecated features that if the emulation version is prior to the introduction of the deprecation AND has no other transitions, the feature default state is on.

We're inconsistent enough with polarity, and with whether the behavior change happens in the very first release a deprecation gate is introduced, that I'm skeptical we can reliably derive a correct default value prior to the gate introduction for gates that show up as deprecated.

we *can* (and probably should) write a unit test that catches gates that show up in new minors as deprecated from the start and guides people to create something like a synthetic entry at "1.0" or "0.0" or something with a default that matches the pre-gated behavior

@siyuanfoundation what linters and/or unit tests do we already have that check for invalid versioned feature gates?   We should start listing out all the things that "should never happen" and start putting up protections to prevent those.

Some that are actively being discussed or have come up in the past:

- Should not be able to have two entries for the same version
- Should not be able to accidentally transition backward in stability levels? At least not without a good reason and without some sort of "ACK, this is what I really want to do".
-  Should not be able to deprecate a GA feature? (or at least, not accientally)
- ???
I was playing around with linting and requiring initial state indication for deprecated gates with something like https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/128947

> We're inconsistent enough with polarity, and with whether the behavior change happens in the very first release a deprecation gate is introduced, that I'm skeptical we can reliably derive a correct default value prior to the gate introduction for gates that show up as deprecated.

SIG Docs came to the same conclusion when changing https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/command-line-tools-reference/feature-gates/ to be rendered based on data.

> I was playing around with linting and requiring initial state indication for deprecated gates with something like https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/128947

xref: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/126893 (which was supposed to be tracked while allowing the current thing to merge late in the release as-is to prevent delaying the functionality, we would really like to avoid a proliferation of DIY static analysis framework(s) if possible)

>

> * Should not be able to accidentally transition backward in stability levels? At least not without a good reason and without some sort of "ACK, this is what I really want to do".
> * Should not be able to deprecate a GA feature? (or at least, not accientally)
> * ???

The linter is only for checking all new features adopt the new versioned format. Now that all the features have been migrated, we actually do not need the linter anymore. 
Long term, I think https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/128947 is a better approach than linter/unit test, because it is ensuring all features follow the same rules, not just limited to k/k.

> The linter is only for checking all new features adopt the new versioned format. Now that all the features have been migrated, we actually do not need the linter anymore.

I agree from a linting perspective, though https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/128241 is an alternative where we can generate a static fixture so that the feature gates in the kubernetes website can be automatically generated rather than having manual PRs that can have drift with the k/k feature set. Obviously its purpose isn't for linting, but the artifact would loosely follow `versioned_feature_list.yaml`

> > The linter is only for checking all new features adopt the new versioned format. Now that all the features have been migrated, we actually do not need the linter anymore.

Obviously its purpose isn't for linting, but the artifact would loosely follow `versioned_feature_list.yaml`

that's a good point, #128241 is useful for doc generation, but we should consider renaming it to reflect the repurpose.
